inputs.userGoal: then lets go with the github deployment nw
subGoals: Bootstrap only the destination network through a manually dispatched GitHub workflow.
Retain the source subscription, VPN, router and current application release configuration.
Require destination-scoped IAM and ARM validation before incurring gateway charges.
insightsApplied: destination-vpn-network: preserve the verified address plan and reserve all four subnets.
destination-vpn-gateway: preserve VpnGw1AZ, OpenVPN, BGP and certificate authentication; use the documented Generation1 pairing for new VpnGw1AZ creation rather than source-reported Generation2.
destination-vpn-public-ip: create a new zone-redundant Standard public IP and retain the source endpoint.
destination-vpn-identity: reuse existing OIDC authentication only after Contributor is granted on the destination group.

reasoning.whyChosen: New isolated migration group with the same name as the source to minimize later configuration changes.
reasoning.tradeoffs: An IAM administrator must create the group and grant the existing GitHub infrastructure identity Contributor here before a group-scoped workflow can run.

reasoning.whyChosen: Reuse the reviewed VNet module and baseline; no NSG or default route on GatewaySubnet.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Identical source and destination CIDRs must not be connected on the same client concurrently. DNS resolver and workload endpoints are later migration stages.

reasoning.whyChosen: Standard static zone-redundant IPv4 pairs with VpnGw1AZ.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A public VPN ingress endpoint is necessary; the destination address differs from the source.

reasoning.whyChosen: Preserve the current client protocol, public root certificate, BGP and zone-redundant SKU using the documented generation pairing for new creation.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Additional hourly charges apply while both gateways exist. No client keys, router changes, source deletion or workload migration are included.

overallReasoning.summary: Isolated GitHub-only first-stage network bootstrap using existing reviewed Bicep modules.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Reuse module API versions to avoid unrelated source-stack changes. A public VPN ingress is required; public root certificates are not secrets. No PaaS services or Key Vault are needed at this stage. Monitoring, private DNS, DNS resolver, application migration and source retirement are explicitly deferred. Missing destination IAM blocks Azure preview/deployment until an administrator provisions the group and role.

plan.validation: Require local Bicep compilation and template boundary checks; GitHub must authenticate to the pinned destination, verify the template with ARM, preview, and accept only the three declared destination resource types plus nested deployment records. Verify gateway provisioning after deployment; physical VPN testing is a separate acceptance gate.
